subject: Archaeology
title: The Laetoli Footprints
description: Learn The Laetoli Footprints in one minute.

hook.text: In Tanzania, 3.6-million-year-old footprints show two early humans walking side by side through volcanic ash.

buildup.text: Mary Leakey discovered the prints in 1978. They were preserved when wet ash from a nearby eruption hardened like cement.

discovery.text: The prints have arches and forward-pointing toes — unmistakable signs of upright bipedal walking.

twist.text: A smaller third set of tracks suggests a child was walking alongside the adults. A family stroll, 3.6 million years ago.

climax.text: These are the oldest confirmed footprints of human ancestors — half a million years older than Lucy.

punchline.text: A family walked through ash 3.6 million years ago.

quiz.question: How were the Laetoli footprints preserved?
options: They were carved into rock by flowing water
Wet volcanic ash hardened like cement around the impressions
They were covered by a layer of mud during a flood
